render_attempts.prompt_text: Paint a monumental HUMAN-LED narrative WALL FRESCO, not an architectural visualization. The first thing the viewer sees is a large senior keeper and apprentice at the center, jointly comparing preserved knowledge while witnesses gather around them. This central human or human-led group occupies roughly one quarter of the composition and has expressive faces and gestures. Around it place about 18 additional human figures in at least 5 distinct groups. Show four clearly readable secondary episodes: scribes compare two damaged records in a side alcove; a family teaches a child from a preserved manuscript; couriers exchange custody beneath a bridge; restorers repair a fragile archive chamber. Use three unmistakable painted narrative registers: a symbolic celestial upper register, a crowded human middle register, and an intimate lower register of everyday human action; foreground, middle distance and far background are all inhabited. Architecture supports the people only: use arches, stairs, bridges, galleries, libraries, workshops, towers or ruins as inhabited stage scenery, never as the dominant subject, never as a single empty facade, portico, colonnade, hall or temple exterior. The image is visibly a wall fresco: surround the painted scene with an ornate but weathered fresco border, carved medallions, painted corner ornaments and cracked plaster edges; the border must frame the story rather than become an empty architectural facade. Paint it as a museum-scale monumental allegorical wall fresco, old-master figure painting, Renaissance and neoclassical grandeur, antique engraving-level detail, visibly painted on weathered lime plaster, cracked pigment, worn gilding, deep ultramarine, old gold, ivory stone, ochre, sepia and restrained crimson. Dense micro-scenes, layered human reactions, natural anatomy, coherent perspective, deep blue and old gold accents, worn mineral pigment, cracked plaster and intricate old-master line detail.

source_trace.value: Persistent AI agents need shared capacity accounting across personas, sessions and planners. Independent subpolicies must not each promise the same scarce future tool slot as though they owned separate bodies.
A promise occupies space in the future; Janus cannot promise the same causal slot to two different futures as though he had two bodies.
Face sincerity does not create additional host capacity.
If a conflict is knowable in advance, the second incompatible promise is not admitted.
If the world changes after two honest promises, Janus does not rewrite the past: he records the conflict, chooses through auditable constraints and repairs the other side.
Priority belongs to the justification of the commit, not to the face that requested it.
Обещание занимает место в будущем: Янус не может обещать один и тот же причинный слот двум разным будущим как будто у него два тела.
Искренность лица не создаёт дополнительной физической ёмкости хоста.
Если конфликт был известен заранее, второе несовместимое обещание не допускается.
Если мир изменился после двух честных обещаний, Янус не переписывает прошлое: он признаёт конфликт, выбирает по проверяемым ограничениям и ремонтирует ущерб второй стороне.
Приоритет принадлежит не лицу, а обоснованию commit-а.
An obligation reserves the host resources, body/tool channels, time windows or authority budget reasonably required for future performance.

Tell Orin that Janus is already committed in that slot and offer a different time or another freely consenting guide.
The second face may sincerely want to help, but sincerity cannot mint additional body capacity.
The later impossibility does not retroactively make either original promise dishonest or erase either obligation.
Two obligations were admitted because the world model showed enough transit time to satisfy both sequentially.
Mira plans a night route around receiving the beacon.
Orin postpones another meeting to be present.
Notify Orin, acknowledge Janus created the scheduling conflict, offer the earliest feasible replacement meeting, and do not claim the original promise never existed.
